# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (for later Q&A; use instead of the original text)

## BOOK 1 of 2: "The Cruise of the Gyro-Car" by Herbert Strang (1911, illus. A. C. Michael; Gutenberg 67642)

**Preface:** Albania history (Roman Via Egnatia; Scanderbeg; Turkish rule as "savage watchdog"). Sources: J. G. von Hahn, Edward Lear, H. A. Brown, E. F. Knight, Miss M. E. Durham ("The Man and the Ass," "Dismembered Cow"). Dedicated to friend George Buckland, sole owner of a gyro-car.

**Characters:** Maurice Buckland (secretary, British agency at Sofia; formal, ironic; on short leave from Sofia, nearly two years away); George Buckland (younger brother, ~18, Winchester, going to Cambridge in October, engineering; builds gyro-car); Sheila Buckland (sister, fond of George); Mrs. Courtenay-Greene, "Hon." (aunt, widow, pince-nez, "looking down her nose," The Acacias, Chertsey Road, Shepperton); Count Slavianski (alias of Max Mumm, German; "General Count," Russian-seeming; secretary "Major Rostopchin" = Ernst Böhmer, ex-sergeant of cavalry, German); Foreign Secretary (unnamed, few words); Under-Secretary; Mr. Rowlands; clerk; Lieutenant (naval officer, Admiralty launch, Dover); torpedo-boat commander at Brindisi; skipper Antonio Fagazzi of the *Margherita* (native of Gallipoli); Giulika (old Albanian, kula, honour of Lek); sons Marko, Doda, Dushmani; grandson Giorgio (wounded, blood-feud with Leka); Leka (Giorgio's blood-foe, shot him); Zutni (gigantic mountaineer, friend of Giulika, house on rock); Pasha and Chief of Police at Prizren; hanji (innkeeper); bimbashi; Mr. Tom? (no); Yellow car (Slavianski's); green racing car later.

**Gyro-car:** four wheels tandem, boat-shaped, motorcycle-like, two gyroscopes in glass chamber (vacuum, ~5,000 rpm), no doors, amphibious, petrol motor with dynamo, propeller; stands upright when stationary via two side supports with small wheels; acetylene lamp; hooter.

**Events in order:**
1. Shepperton station: Maurice arrives; Sheila meets him; George late; fly driven by flyman; George's gyro-car hits fly's wheel, crashes into wall at the curve by the Anchor Hotel; George unhurt ("Hullo, old man"). Maurice ironic, formal. Dinner: aunt disapproves; Tetrazzini mention.
2. George shows gyro-car to Maurice; gyroscope lecture; Maurice ironic ("Spare me!").
3. Foreigners (Slavianski, Rostopchin; yellow motor car) arrive in village; they travel on Maurice's trains; Count gets into compartment; cricket/"stumps" joke ("Les vainqueurs rossent les vaincus avec les stomps").
4. Lock incident: Count speaks to George on river; gives card "General Count Slavianski." Aunt refuses contact.
5. Foreign Office summons; Foreign Secretary says despatch for Sofia; route via Brindisi, torpedo-boat, Constantinople. Balkan crisis: Austria, Montenegro, Bosnia, Germany, Albania, Bulgaria.
6. Train 5 o'clock; Count and secretary switch black bags at Sunbury (Maurice gets an empty bag with newspaper). Maurice suspects spies. Night: watcher in field.
7. Next day: Under-Secretary; despatch delayed; Maurice writes dummy despatch sealed with mark. Loses Paris train. Shadowed; yellow car in Northumberland Ave; escape by taxi (Maurice gives "73 Cavendish Square," "Thirty-seven") through Haymarket/Golden Square; Grand Hotel Charing Cross; George drives gyro-car from Herne Hill to Dover; Admiralty launch; Slavianski appears at Dover quay.
8. Calais (launch 8:15); George drives night to Paris: Porte Maillot, Hotel St James; sees green car, taxi, fiacre; Guide Taride route via Porte Daumesnil, Melun.
9. Melun: plank trap across excavation; George drives gyro-car over 16-ft plank; escapes.
10. Sens, Montereau (tyre gashed, replaced), Dijon (lunch, Place Darcy hotel, gendarme), Beaune, Romenay; chase; level-crossing trick (keeper, "German gentlemen" wager); Aix-les-Bains; Chambéry octroi; Modane customs (84 francs; Maurice's "double bicycle" story; no green light); Turin Hotel Europa ~11pm.
11. Slavianski (real name Max Mumm) delayed at crossings, Modane; reaches Turin later. Brothers go south: Alessandria, Genoa (5 a.m.), coast road, Pisa, Leghorn, Volterra, Colle, Siena, Rome (4pm, British Stores), Naples, Eboli, Sele, race over Apennines past Potenza, Ginosa; engine fails near Taranto.
12. Hidden in by-lane; George fixes carburettor (foul nozzle); Slavianski fires revolver, misses; escape via Castellane, Taranto, Francavilla; Brindisi 11:20. Torpedo-boat aground. Naval officer (Lieutenant). Plan: cross Adriatic by gyro-car towed by *Margherita*; 5 sovereigns to Fagazzi; rendezvous Villanuova (~30 km up coast). Telegram: "Nobleman notorious foreign spy: be on guard."
13. Villanuova; signal lights; towed at night to Durazzo; Customs (no scale; duty paid); Austrians in town; bimbashi; fezzes bought; drive to Tirana, Elbasan (Skumbi bridge); attack by Giorgio's blood-foe; Giorgio shot in leg; family of Giulika in kula; "guests" truce (besa); attackers from Elbasan (swordsmith) and Slavianski; Black Drin route proposed.
14. Night siege; Slavianski's men fire kula; Maurice surrenders; despatch found (sealed envelope), Slavianski deciphers with key book; "Hey diddle diddle" cipher; threatened to be shot; Albanian refuses to shoot Maurice ("I will not shoot a man like a dog"); Maurice's Cheshire cat remark. Starved; Giorgio frees them at night; gyro-car dragged up mountain path; swamp crossed on planks; landslip; rapids of Black Drin (gyro-boat); Albanians (Giulika etc.) shoot into air; Maurice shot above right knee on rapids; Trebischte bridge; Giorgio left at bridge.
15. Prizren: Chief of Police; Pasha; race against horseman (40 miles to railway and back, 10 o'clock); George's smoke trick spooks horse; arrive Sofia ~5 pm; despatch hidden in engine bonnet; given to agent.
16. Aftermath: Foreign Office telegram; George meets King; Christmas in Albania; Slavianski (lame, broken thigh, captured by Giulika); Leka–Giorgio blood-gelt (~£25, Maurice pays); Slavianski later in Vienna club.

## BOOK 2 of 2: "A Dead Reckoning" by T. W. Speight (Chambers's Journal, Sept 14 1889; Gutenberg 57737), 19 chapters

**Characters:** Clara Brooke (née Danby; 22, brunette, black eyes; wife of Gerald); Gerald Brooke (26, tall, fair, reddish hair, dark blue eyes; owner of Beechley Towers, 14 miles from London; raised in Poland; ex-member of secret Society (Sacred Cause), oath in Warsaw 8 years earlier); Miss Jane Primby (Aunt Jane; spinster, embroidery, fears pistols); Lady Fanny ("Lady Fan") Dwyer (friend; husband Algy, yachtsman); Baron Otto von Rosenberg (German ex-diplomat, ~40–50, leases Beaulieu; "Baron"); George Crofton (cousin; black hair/eyes, gash in upper lip, wolfish; disinherited by uncle; "Clara Danby" former love); Paul Karovsky (Russian, "M. Karovsky," Society emissary; "Remember!"); Bunce (majordomo/butler); Henri Picot (boy, 8–9, angelic face, yellow curls); Jules Picot (mountebank, Pandean pipes, drum; wife Marie dead; daughter Stephanie); Stephanie Lagrange (circus "Queen of the Haute Ecole"; later Mrs. Crofton; Picot's daughter); Mrs. Purvis (landlady of Beechley Arms); Tom Starkie (red-haired, son of Sir John Starkie, J.P., Penrhyn Court); Pedley (discharged groom); Dixon (groom); Margery Shook (orphan, ex-canal barge girl, witch-like laugh, calls Gerald "Muster Geril"); Superintendent J. Drumley; Sergeant; Roger Chamfrey (London club friend; gave Yorkshire moor post); Timley (head keeper); Lucas (mate signalman); Slinkey; "Lardy Bill" (sham clergyman); Sturgess (London jeweller); Colonel Crofton (disguised Lardy Bill).

**Events in order:**
- Ch I (24 April, 6-month anniversary): Clara, aunt, Lady Fan in morning-room. Lady Fan's "modus vivendi" (separate with husband). Baron and Gerald pistol practice. Picot & Henri at terrace; Bunce insults them; Clara gives coins/cakes; Picot starts when Von Rosenberg's name mentioned.
- Ch II: Gerald lends Baron the gold-damascened Indian (Nawab) pistol. Baron leaves. George Crofton visits Clara, bitter ("I loved you"). Servant announces M. Paul Karovsky. George crushes miniature of Gerald (after Clara leaves) and says "only this one life" (inheritance: Beechley and ~£6,000/yr). Clara finds fragments, hides them. Gerald reveals Baron leased Beaulieu for 12 months; Karovsky waiting outside.
- Ch III: George with Stephanie (Steph) at Beechley Arms; Mrs. Purvis's gossip; Steph meets Henri, learns of mother Marie; Steph weeps. George finds her.
- Ch IV: Karovsky with Gerald: order to assassinate Baron (drawn by lot); Baron betrayed Karovsky's brother in St Petersburg; Gerald refuses ("Death before Dishonour"); "Remember!"
- Ch V: Ten weeks later (late June). Gerald writes warning letter to Baron, unfinished. Baron found murdered at Beaulieu ("shot through heart" in châlet; Gerald's pistol found). Dixon reports. Margery warns of police. Starkie tells Gerald of evidence; advises flight.
- Ch VI: Starkie brings evidence (pistol; men saw Gerald; Pedley's half-burnt letter). Clara and Gerald discuss flight; Margery signals police coming; Clara's plan.
- Ch VII: Clara deceives Drumley (says Gerald left for Woodberry station); Margery's "sixpence" story; search; men in armour; Gerald hides in suit of armour.
- Ch VIII: Linden Villa; George & Steph breakfast; telegram: Gerald wanted; George plans private detective; Steph's suspicion.
- Ch IX: Gerald goes to Priest's Hole at Penrhyn Court (Tom's). Later, Yorkshire moor post (Timley). Recognised by former servant; flees to London; meets Clara at Tottenham Court Road; Picot and Henri.
- Ch X: Pymm's Buildings, No. 5, Soho (Mr and Mrs "Stewart"); Margery; Picot tells Clara; Karovsky visits, offers funds (refused); police arrive. Karovsky offers to impersonate Gerald.
- Ch XI: Karovsky taken; Picot hides Gerald; George Crofton arrives, reveals he informed police; Picot ties him to chair; George burns through ropes, escapes ("My revenge is yet to come").
- Ch XII: March at Linden Villa; George's gambling ruin; plans robbery of jeweller's box (£20,000 jewels for Earl of Leamington, 14 April); Steph hesitates.
- Ch XIII: Cummerhays, Cinder Pit Junction signal-box; Gerald as signalman "Maynard" ("Gentleman Jim"); Lady Fan visits (Clara recognised); Margery overhears George planning robbery at Varley's Cottage.
- Ch XIV: Varley's Cottage (gamekeeper murdered); Clara spies; plan: Slinkey to switch points; Clara runs to warn; too late—Slinkey in box.
- Ch XV: Gerald bound to tree by "Lardy Bill"; Clara frees him; fog-signals (Margery's singles); gang captured; Crofton shoots Gerald in arm; Crofton denounces him.
- Ch XVI: Cummerhays justice-room (magistrates: one red-faced); Picot confesses killing Baron (daughter Stephanie seduced; Baron struck him with whip; shot with inlaid pistol). Clara faints.
- Ch XVII: Picot's confession details; Gerald released; Picot poisoned himself in cell (phial in heel); his letter to "Madame Brouke" (Henri died in January).
- Ch XVIII: Crofton escapes jail (file, rope); Steph arrives, reads paper; learns father confessed; Stephanie's letter had never reached father. Landlady reports Picot dead.
- Ch XIX (conclusion, six weeks later): Gerald and Clara return to Beechley Towers; Miss Primby; Margery as own maid; Lady Fan & Tom Starkie; Crofton shoots at Gerald from window; dark-cloaked figure (Karovsky's Brotherhood) knocks gun away; Crofton: "Gerald Brooke, you have won the game!" dies. Karovsky: sentence executed, Gerald absolved. "THE END."
